household: with Larry Slade, Hugo Kalmar and the other roomers
creator: Eugene O'Neill
address_as_given: a five-story tenement-type rooming house over a saloon on the downtown West Side, across from the Market
notes: Hope and his roomers (Larry Slade, Hugo Kalmar, Willie Oban and others) live upstairs. O'Neill drew on real dives he knew, but which one is debated and I did not verify it here. The play sets Hope's on the downtown West Side, across the street from "the Market people" and near the waterfront, which points to the Washington Market district. O'Neill drew it from several bars he knew: Jimmy-the-Priest's at 252 Fulton Street on the waterfront, the Golden Swan (the Hell Hole) at Sixth Avenue and West 4th Street, and the Garden Hotel taproom. The mark follows the play's text rather than the Village models.
source_quote: The Iceman Cometh is set in New York in 1912 in Harry Hope's downmarket Greenwich Village saloon and rooming house.
source2_quote: a cheap ginmill of the five-cent whiskey, last-resort variety situated on the downtown West Side of New York.
